newsitem.title: LEBANON: Beirut says awaits Clinton action on Mideast talks.
newsitem.headline: Beirut says awaits Clinton action on Mideast talks.

text.p: Lebanon said on Wednesday that it awaited action by re-elected U.S. President Bill Clinton on stalled Arab-Israeli peace talks.

Lebanese Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri, asked by reporters how Clinton's re-election reflects on the peace talks, said: "This depends on the American stand over the peace process." He did not elaborate.

Later, Foreign Minister Faris Bouez said after meeting U.S. ambassador in Beirut Richard Jones that at this stage it was premature to have too much optimism that the United States could pressure Israel.

"It is better to see how President Clinton will act at the start of his second term and how the formula will be in Congress and how that will allow the American president to take stands that his responsibilities as the head of a superpower dictate," Bouez told reporters.

More than five years of on-again off-again peace talks between Lebanon and Israel have produced no results. The main bone of contention is Israel's occupation of a border zone in south Lebanon to ward off cross-frontier guerrilla raids.
